Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.02 U06 L05 GP Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.02 Perspective: Source checks help students choose stronger research evidence. Which slide note is clearest? \

answer.text: A. Stuff about sources and research

feedback.text: Incorrect. This wording is vague and would not help the audience understand the evidence.

answer.text: B. Sources can be on websites and in other places.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is broad and does not explain the source-checking strategy.

answer.text: C. Check author, date, and purpose before using a source.

feedback.text: Correct. This slide note is concise, clear, and connected to the presentation perspective.

answer.text: D. Research is something students do in school.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too general and does not support the specific perspective.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.RS.01 U06 L05 GP Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.RS.01 Which evidence source is most credible for a digital presentation about student research habits? \

answer.text: A. A random anonymous comment online

feedback.text: Incorrect. Anonymous comments are difficult to verify and are weak evidence for an academic presentation.

answer.text: B. A friend's guess about research habits

feedback.text: Incorrect. A guess is not reliable enough to support a digital presentation.

answer.text: C. A school survey showing how students choose online sources

feedback.text: Correct. A school survey is relevant and provides evidence connected to the presentation topic.

answer.text: D. A joke about students searching the internet

feedback.text: Incorrect. A joke is not reliable research evidence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.W.04 U06 L05 GP Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.V.01 Weak slide note: The research source thing is helpful because people can see whether source stuff is good. Which revision is clearest? \

answer.text: A. Source checks help students judge whether evidence is reliable.

feedback.text: Correct. This revision is concise, clear, and uses precise language.

answer.text: B. People can look at the thing and know stuff.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This wording is still unclear and informal.

answer.text: C. Source stuff is good for many things.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This remains vague and does not improve clarity.

answer.text: D. Research is research when people research it.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is circular and does not explain the idea.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.V.01 U06 L05 GP Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.W.04 Which phrase uses academic vocabulary appropriately for a slide about evidence? \

answer.text: A. pretty good source stuff

feedback.text: Incorrect. This phrase is informal and vague.

answer.text: B. credible evidence from a reliable source

feedback.text: Correct. This phrase uses precise academic vocabulary appropriate for the topic.

answer.text: C. random facts from somewhere

feedback.text: Incorrect. This phrase suggests weak evidence and lacks precision.

answer.text: D. things that help maybe

feedback.text: Incorrect. This wording is too uncertain and unclear.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.02 U06 L05 GP Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.02 A slide has a full paragraph of evidence copied onto it. What is the best revision choice? \

answer.text: A. Add another full paragraph to balance the slide.

feedback.text: Incorrect. More text would make the slide harder to read.

answer.text: B. Remove all evidence from the presentation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Evidence is still needed; it should be presented clearly.

answer.text: C. Make the paragraph smaller so more words fit.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Smaller text does not solve the clarity problem.

answer.text: D. Use a concise evidence note on the slide and explain the evidence orally.

feedback.text: Correct. This keeps the slide clear while preserving the support.
